title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
technique: Context-free-grammar constrained decoding: adaptive token-mask cache for context-independent tokens, persistent stack, grammar-computation overlapped with GPU execution

optimized_metrics.evidence: to minimize the overhead of constrained decoding.
Finally, we co-designed the grammar ... engine with LLM inference engines to overlap the grammar ... computations with GPU computations, bringing minimal ... overhead for structured generation.

headline_claim.text: XGrammar can achieve up to 100x reduction in per-token latency for context-free grammar compared to current state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, the XGrammar-integrated LLM serving engine for Llama3.1 models achieves up to an 80x speedup in end-to-end LLM serving with structured output on the H100 GPU.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Efficiency is measured by the average time per output token (TPOT), which reflects the overhead of applying constraints during token generation.
metric_definitions.notes: Mean TPOT in ms in online serving with fixed batch sizes (1, 8, 16, 32...), H100, Llama-3.1-8B; input avg 139 tokens, output avg 53 tokens; fixed maximum output length.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: XGrammar consistently achieves the lowest latency across all tasks, with under 40 µs per token for JSON Schema and CFG (JSON), and under 200 µs for XML and Python DSL.
metric_definitions.notes: CPU time to generate the token mask per decoding step (grammar engine only, no LLM), RTX 4090 setup; separate from end-to-end TPOT.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We compare the time to first token (TTFT) and time per output token (TPOT) between structured generation with XGrammar and non-structured generation while ensuring the number of generated tokens is the same.
metric_definitions.notes: Overhead measured as the ratio vs unstructured generation; used (not defined) in browser/iPhone experiments.

extractor_notes: Not an agent-scheduling paper: structured generation engine where the objective is per-token constraint overhead (microseconds mask time and TPOT overhead), i.e. a TOKEN_LAT / TPOT-overhead metric, not request latency. Two different 'latencies': Fig 9 per-token mask time (us) vs Fig 10 end-to-end TPOT (ms). Batch sizes fixed, no tails.
